proposals.stance: Most agent demos die because nobody owns them after launch; an agent needs a named owner to reach day thirty.
proposals.why_we_believe_it: Our new post on agent ownership says the agents that last are the ones someone is accountable for after launch, and our demos post says the test is day thirty. Together they put the cause on ownership, not on the model.

evidence.quote: The agents that survive are the ones with a named owner after launch.
A demo that works once is not an agent; an agent is the thing that still works on day thirty.

proposals.applies_when: A company launches an agent with no word on who runs it afterwards, or a survey reports agent projects being abandoned.
proposals.counter_position: Demos die because models are not good enough yet. Model quality matters, but we see good models fail in teams where nobody owns the agent.
proposals.never_say: That model quality does not matter.
proposals.answers_note: Too soft. We'd say most demos die because nobody owns them after launch.
